_about: Hand-maintained figures for the Railbelt natural gas page (/natural-gas/). Edit a value and commit; the page redraws from this file. EIA monthly prices come separately from data/natural-gas.json, written by scripts/fetch_data.py.

gca._note: Enstar's Gas Cost Adjustment: its average cost of gas, passed through to customers at cost. Reset each July for the year to June. Add the new year after Enstar's May filing.
gca.source: Enstar tariff filings with the Regulatory Commission of Alaska (TA345-4, TA355-4) and Enstar's June 2026 bill insert

ladder._note: What the next Mcf of gas could cost. lo/hi for ranges; value for a single figure. Dollars per thousand cubic feet unless noted.

rows.label: LNG imported through a new Nikiski terminal
rows.sub: Enstar's estimate for 2033: $15 if Enstar is the only user, $13 if all utilities share it

rows.label: Imported LNG, ISER's range
rows.sub: Pacific LNG prices over the past decade, plus about $1 for shipping and $3–5 for the terminal

rows.label: North Slope gas through the Alaska LNG pipeline
rows.sub: Price cap in a 30-year contract Glenfarne and Enstar were negotiating, $16 per million Btu plus inflation

rows.label: Enstar's offer for new Cook Inlet gas
rows.sub: Standing offer to any producer, July 2026; no takers reported

demand.label: Oil fields, refinery and other industry

contracts.label: Enstar
contracts.sub: Gas for about 150,000 homes and businesses; also supplies Homer Electric
contracts.note: Hilcorp firm contract, 28 Bcf a year plus 4.4 Bcf of options, ends March 2033

contracts.label: Matanuska Electric
contracts.note: Hilcorp contract through March 2029; Enstar will buy MEA's gas after that

new_supply.label: Alaska LNG pipeline, first gas target

supply.source: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil and Gas, legislative presentations Jan 2026; AOGCC production data via Petroleum News

items.text: Enstar told legislators it was about 3 billion cubic feet short for the winter, roughly 18 days of normal winter demand. Last winter's record cold drained its storage, and two expected supplies fell through.
Matanuska Electric told nearly 60,000 members that rolling outages of up to 45 minutes were possible in a worst case. Chugach Electric said it was not planning outages.

Gas from BlueCrest's Cosmopolitan field, expected to reach Enstar in September, did not arrive. BlueCrest says it has funding for a new well that could produce about 25 million cubic feet a day as soon as 2027.

Regulators approved a 1.2 billion cubic foot exchange: Hilcorp sells Enstar gas set aside for Matanuska Electric, and Enstar pays MEA back in gas by March 2028. Without it, Enstar expected about 3.7 billion cubic feet in storage at the end of December.

Enstar said its stored gas is still below normal for this time of year. Forecasts call for a warmer winter than last, but it is planning for cold. If gas runs short, power plants are affected first; the first step would likely be asking MEA to run its Eklutna plant on diesel.

projects.name: More wells in existing fields
projects.what: Hilcorp has drilled 192 Cook Inlet wells since 2011, 27 of them in 2026. Furie doubled Kitchen Lights output in 2025 and plans up to nine more wells; HEX says it will deliver 26 million cubic feet a day firm to Enstar by April 2027.

projects.name: Cosmopolitan gas
projects.what: A new well near Anchor Point, about 25 million cubic feet a day. The state has warned BlueCrest it could lose the unit for missing deadlines.

projects.name: Kenai LNG import terminal
projects.what: Convert the idle Nikiski LNG export plant to receive imported LNG. Estimated $300–350 million; permits sought for about 20 billion cubic feet a year.

projects.name: Cook Inlet Gateway import terminal
projects.what: A new terminal at Nikiski, about 300 million cubic feet a day, designed to become part of an Alaska LNG export plant later.
projects.when: 2029 at the earliest; Enstar expects to need imports by 2033

projects.name: Floating import terminal
projects.what: Moor a floating storage and regasification ship at the Osprey platform on the west side of the inlet.

projects.name: Alaska LNG pipeline, phase one
projects.what: A 739-mile, 42-inch pipeline from the North Slope to Southcentral. North Slope producers have signed supply agreements; South Korea announced more than $50 billion of investment in September 2026.

projects.name: Federal offshore lease sales
projects.what: Congress requires annual Cook Inlet lease sales from 2026 to 2028 and 2030 to 2032. The first, in March 2026, drew no bids.
